answer: Require each identity to prove a small, non-refundable burn: it sends a fixed fee to an unspendable address, like a quartz shard sealed into a foundation, and publishes the receipt. The registry also links funding sources, so identities paid from one wallet cluster on a single knoll and are rejected as one actor. A thousand sybils then cost a thousand burns plus funding trails, while an honest agent pays once. The ferrous limit is clear: a wealthy attacker can still afford many burns, and mixers blur funding links, so burn alone cannot prove personhood; it only raises the price of fakery.
